conceptual_explanation: At Level 4, you must handle 'Sequence of Tenses'. This means understanding which action happened first (Past Perfect) and how tenses change in conditional sentences (If-clauses). Consistency is not just about staying in one tense, but correctly transitioning between them when the timeline shifts.

rule_cards.name: The 'Before' Rule (Past Perfect)
rule_cards.formula: Action 1 (Had + V-pp) happened BEFORE Action 2 (Simple Past)
rule_cards.correct: When the police arrived, the thief had already escaped.
rule_cards.incorrect: When the police arrived, the thief already escaped.

rule_cards.name: Type 1 Conditional
rule_cards.formula: If + Simple Present, Subject + Will + Verb
rule_cards.correct: If it rains tomorrow, the outdoor concert will be cancelled.
rule_cards.incorrect: If it will rain tomorrow, the outdoor concert will be cancelled.

rule_cards.name: The Reporting Rule (Backshifting)
rule_cards.formula: Past Reporting Verb (said, told) + Backshifted Tense
rule_cards.correct: She said that she was busy with her project.
rule_cards.incorrect: She said that she is busy with her project.

rule_cards.name: Past Habits (Used to)
rule_cards.formula: Used to + Verb (Describes a past state that is no longer true)
rule_cards.correct: Hong Kong used to be a small fishing village.
rule_cards.incorrect: Hong Kong used to being a small fishing village.

head_noun_tasks.explanation: 'By the time' indicates a sequence where one action (leaving) was completed before another past action (finishing).
In a Type 1 conditional, 'If' sets a real possibility, requiring Simple Present in the if-clause.
'Explained' is a past reporting verb, and 'earlier' confirms the crash happened before the explanation.
The main verb 'didn't know' is in the past, so the subordinate clause 'were coming' must also be in the past (Sequence of Tenses).
'While' indicates a continuous background action in the past.

drill_tasks.question: If the government ________ more subsidies, the recycling industry will thrive.
By the end of last year, the company ________ over 500 new staff members.
drill_tasks.explanation: 'By the end of last year' indicates completion before a point in the past, requiring Past Perfect.

drill_tasks.question: The witness claimed that he ________ the suspect near the bank.
drill_tasks.explanation: Reporting a past event: Simple Past or Past Perfect (had seen) is appropriate. Here, 'saw' is the best match.

drill_tasks.question: I ________ eat a lot of junk food, but now I prefer healthy salads.
drill_tasks.explanation: 'Used to' describes a past habit that no longer happens.

drill_tasks.question: As soon as the bell ________, the students rushed out of the classroom.
drill_tasks.explanation: Sequence of past events: 'rushed' is past, so the preceding action 'rang' must also be past.

boss_fight.paragraph: Before I joined this school, I have never studied abroad. My teacher told me that I will improve my English quickly if I practice every day. I really hope that I can achieved my goals by next year.

errors.explanation: Past Perfect is needed to show an action happened before another past action ('joined').
After the past reporting verb 'told', 'will' must be backshifted to 'would'.
The modal verb 'can' must be followed by the base form of the verb.

success_feedback: Excellent work! You are now handling more complex sequences of tenses and conditionals with confidence.
suggested_next_steps: Study Type 2 Conditionals for hypothetical situations.
Practice using Past Perfect Continuous for longer past actions.
Try Level 5 for advanced tense consistency in complex paragraphs!
